items.source: In order to support asynchronous requests and error dispatches this filter should be mapped with DispatcherType.ASYNC and also DispatcherType.ERROR. However if registering the filter via web.xml or in Spring Boot via a FilterRegistrationBean be sure to include DispatcherType.ASYNC and DispatcherType.ERROR in addition to DispatcherType.REQUEST.

items.source: OncePerRequestFilter — extension of GenericFilterBean that supports a single invocation at the start of a request, i.e. during the REQUEST dispatch phase, and ignoring further handling via FORWARD dispatches. items.source: The spring-web module provides FormContentFilter to intercept HTTP PUT, PATCH, and DELETE requests with a content type of application/x-www-form-urlencoded, read the form data from the body of the request, and wrap the ServletRequest to make the form data available through the ServletRequest.getParameter*() family of methods.

items.source: ForwardedHeaderFilter is a Servlet filter that modifies the request in order to a) change the host, port, and scheme based on Forwarded headers, and b) to remove those headers to eliminate further impact. The filter relies on wrapping the request, and therefore it must be ordered ahead of other filters, such as RequestContextFilter, that should work with the modified and not the original request.
items.translation: ForwardedHeaderFilter is a Servlet filter that modifies the request in order to a) change the host, port, and scheme based on Forwarded headers, and b) to remove those headers to eliminate further impact. The filter relies on wrapping the request, and therefore it must be ordered ahead of other filters, such as RequestContextFilter, that should work with the modified and not the original request.

items.source: There are security considerations for forwarded headers since an application cannot know if the headers were added by a proxy, as intended, or by a malicious client. This is why a proxy at the boundary of trust should be configured to remove untrusted Forwarded headers that come from the outside. You can also configure the ForwardedHeaderFilter with removeOnly=true, in which case it removes but does not use the headers.

items.source: While not standard, X-Forwarded-Host: <host> is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original host to a downstream server. For example, if a request of example.com/resource is sent to a proxy which forwards the request to localhost:8080/resource, then a header of X-Forwarded-Host: example.com can be sent to inform the server that the original host was example.com.
items.translation: While not standard, X-Forwarded-Host: <host> is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original host to a downstream server. For example, if a request of example.com/resource is sent to a proxy which forwards the request to localhost:8080/resource, then a header of X-Forwarded-Host: example.com can be sent to inform the server that the original host was example.com.

items.source: While not standard, X-Forwarded-Proto: (https|http) is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original protocol (for example, https / http) to a downstream server. For example, if a request of example.com/resource is sent to a proxy which forwards the request to localhost:8080/resource, then a header of X-Forwarded-Proto: https can be sent to inform the server that the original protocol was https.
items.translation: While not standard, X-Forwarded-Proto: (https|http) is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original protocol (for example, https / http) to a downstream server. For example, if a request of example.com/resource is sent to a proxy which forwards the request to localhost:8080/resource, then a header of X-Forwarded-Proto: https can be sent to inform the server that the original protocol was https.

items.source: While not standard, X-Forwarded-Port: <port> is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original port to a downstream server. For example, if a request of example.com/resource is sent to a proxy which forwards the request to localhost:8080/resource, then a header of X-Forwarded-Port: 443 can be sent to inform the server that the original port was 443.
items.translation: While not standard, X-Forwarded-Port: <port> is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original port to a downstream server. For example, if a request of example.com/resource is sent to a proxy which forwards the request to localhost:8080/resource, then a header of X-Forwarded-Port: 443 can be sent to inform the server that the original port was 443.

items.source: While not standard, X-Forwarded-Ssl: (on|off) is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original protocol (for example, https / https) to a downstream server. For example, if a request of example.com/resource is sent to a proxy which forwards the request to localhost:8080/resource, then a header of X-Forwarded-Ssl: on to inform the server that the original protocol was https.
items.translation: While not standard, X-Forwarded-Ssl: (on|off) is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original protocol (for example, https / https) to a downstream server. For example, if a request of example.com/resource is sent to a proxy which forwards the request to localhost:8080/resource, then a header of X-Forwarded-Ssl: on to inform the server that the original protocol was https.

items.source: The proxy has no prefix, while applications app1 and app2 have path prefixes /app1 and /app2 respectively. The proxy can send X-Forwarded-Prefix: to have the empty prefix override server prefixes /app1 and /app2.

items.source: The prefix is the start of the path before the capture group {path}. For the proxy, the prefix is /api while for the server the prefix is /app1. In this case, the proxy can send X-Forwarded-Prefix: /api to have the original prefix /api override the server prefix /app1.
items.translation: The prefix is the start of the path before the capture group {path}. For the proxy, the prefix is /api while for the server the prefix is /app1. In this case, the proxy can send X-Forwarded-Prefix: /api to have the original prefix /api override the server prefix /app1.

items.source: In this case, the proxy has a prefix of /api/app1 and the server has a prefix of /app1. The proxy can send X-Forwarded-Prefix: /api/app1 to have the original prefix /api/app1 override the server prefix /app1.

items.source: X-Forwarded-For: <address> is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original InetSocketAddress of the client to a downstream server. For example, if a request is sent by a client at [fd00:fefe:1::4] to a proxy at 192.168.0.1, the "remote address" information contained in the HTTP request will reflect the actual address of the client, not the proxy.
items.translation: X-Forwarded-For: <address> is a de-facto standard header that is used to communicate the original InetSocketAddress of the client to a downstream server. For example, if a request is sent by a client at [fd00:fefe:1::4] to a proxy at 192.168.0.1, the "remote address" information contained in the HTTP request will reflect the actual address of the client, not the proxy.

items.source: RFC 7239 defines the Forwarded HTTP header that proxies can use to provide information about the original request.
